description: The line plot illustrates the performance of four different DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) variants as measured by MRR@10 (Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10) across varying numbers of queries used during inference, ranging from 1 to 10. The x-axis, labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S)”, is linearly scaled from 1 to 10 with integer tick marks. The y-axis, labeled “MRR@10”, spans from 33.0 to 36.0 in increments of 0.5. Four distinct lines represent the methods: “DPR w/o query” (black solid line) remains constant at approximately 34.3 across all S values; “DPR w/ corpus expansion” (red line with circle markers) starts at 35.2 at S=1, rises to a peak of 35.8 at S=6, and then plateaus near 35.8 through S=10; “DPR w/ document expansion” (green line with triangle markers) begins at 34.8, fluctuates slightly around 34.8–34.9, and ends at 34.8 at S=10; and “DPR w/ asymmetric expansion” (blue line with star markers) starts at 34.7, peaks at 35.0 at S=2, dips to 34.6 at S=6, and declines to 34.4 at S=10. The plot visually compares how each expansion strategy responds to increasing the number of inference-time queries.
